new_statements.quote: Vowel length and stress are not contrastive. Preliminary observations would suggest primary stress is placed on the first syllable.7 Understanding how stress placement is affected by verbal morphology, and how stress affects the length of syllables (both stressed and unstressed), requires further research.

Footnote 7 (Klaiman 1987 on Bengali initial stress) is as reported. Surroun…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is non-contrastive; primary stress falls on the first syllable of the word (author's preliminary observation, explicitly hedged). For the [rkt] half of the retired code, Toulmin 2011 (Jazyki mira, p.432 sec. 5.1.1) independently states initial-syllable stress for Cooch Behar Kamta.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; author flags that the effect of verbal morphology on stress placement is unresearched. Toulmin 2009 p.94 notes two Kamta lects (Bongaigaon, Shalkumar) with 'no strong initial stress'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, impressionistic ('preliminary observations'); no phrase-level or citation-form discussion. Statement describes Nepal Rajbanshi (Jhapa/Morang) = rajb1243, one of the two successors of retired [rjb].
new_statements.identity_note: rajb1244 is a Glottolog Bookkeeping languoid for the retired ISO 639-3 code [rjb], split by CR 2007-008 (adopted 2008-01-14) into [rjs] Rajbanshi (Nepal) = rajb1243 and [rkt] Kamta/Rangpuri = rang1265. It denotes no distinct language and has no literature of its own. The quoted statement (Wilde 2008) describes Nepal Rajbanshi = rajb1243, which is ALREADY in the catalog with this exact quote. The Kamta half (rang1265) has its own audit folder with Toulmin 2011 p.432 (initial stress). Adding rajb1244 would duplicate rajb1243; retired codes confer no identity.
